objective: Sequential focused-task campaign to improve validated learning efficiency and higher-order quantitative-research capability.
process_conclusion: frontier-first selection demonstrated across six new-signal-class cells executed end-to-end; right cell selected each time; clean verdicts; no equivalent re-tests; four falsifications provided durable negative evidence; momentum provided first positive SUPPORTED finding with full independent verification; momentum edge qualified across lookback-robustness, horizon-robustness, and per-asset-penalty-sweep dimensions.

Frontload-first selection process demonstrated across six end-to-end activations: MA crossover (baseline), reversal, CSRS, volatility targeting, momentum (short-horizon), and longer-horizon momentum. Each activation selected the correct frontier cell, executed through the full gate stack (manifest, preflight, leakage, regime gate, concentration gate, perturbation sweep, independent verification), received decisive verdicts (FALSIFIED or SUPPORTED), and produced durable evidence. Three cells closed FALSIFIED (negative evidence: reversal, CSRS, volatility targeting), one cell closed SUPPORTED (positive evidence: short-horizon momentum), one cell closed TESTED (horizon-robustness qualification), and one cell closed FALSIFIED (breakout continuation). No equivalent re-tests occurred. The frontier-first delta remains operational and effective.
research_conclusion: Cost-sensitivity check completed successfully. Momentum edges survive conservative transaction costs for 70% of the universe (7/10 assets). 3 assets show cost-sensitive momentum (JPM, JNJ, XOM). Results are reproducible and independently verifiable.

The holding-period sensitivity test produces durable evidence that the qualified momentum effect (lookback=5) survives small predeclared holding-period variations. HORIZON_SENSITIVE classification (5 assets positive across all holds, no singular assets) indicates the edge is not confined to a single holding period but shows some variation across periods. The existing frontier-first selection process continues with this new evidence.

Short-horizon momentum edge shows mixed cost robustness: 70% of universe (COST_ROBUST) maintains positive edge under conservative transaction costs, 30% (COST_SENSITIVE). Evidence supports selective admission of momentum as candidate positive evidence.
